children: Australian shares hit a two-week low on Thursday, led by a sell-off in heavyweight miners, with banks limiting further declines as investors turned cautious after a hot US inflation print stirred bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike.
fell 1% to 8,644.20 points by 2340 GMT, on course for its worst day since the start of October, after falling 0.6% on Wednesday.
The index also touched its lowest level since October 2.
Risk appetite took a hit after US data showed inflation remained stubbornly high, driven by surging energy prices, bolstering bets that the Fed would lean towards another rate hike later this month.

Earlier this week, the Reserve Bank of Australia said it still sees a risk that inflation could prove more stubborn than expected, leaving the door open to a fifth rate hike this year if needed. Markets are pricing in a 65.9% chance the central bank will hold rates at its next meeting, against a 34.1% chance of a hike.
